questions.questionText: Economists regard decision making as important because:

options.text: The resources required to satisfy our unlimited wants and needs are finite, or scarce.
It is crucial to understand how we can best allocate our scarce resources to satisfy society’s unlimited wants and needs.
Resources have alternative uses.
All the above.

questions.explanation: In Business Economics, decision making is essential because productive resources (land, labour, capital) are limited and scarce relative to human wants, and possess alternative uses. Managers must rationally allocate these scarce resources to maximize organizational objectives. Hence, (D) 'All the above.' is the correct choice.

questions.questionText: Business Economics is -

options.text: Abstract and applies the tools of Microeconomics.
Involves practical application of economic theory in business decision making.
Incorporates tools from multiple disciplines.
(b) and (c) above.

questions.explanation: Business Economics (or Managerial Economics) applies microeconomic and macroeconomic theories, quantitative techniques, and business principles to solve practical business problems and formulate forward planning decisions. Hence, (D) '(b) and (c) above.' is the correct answer.

questions.questionText: In Economics, we use the term scarcity to mean -

options.text: Absolute scarcity and lack of resources in less developed countries.
Relative scarcity i.e. scarcity in relation to the wants of the society.
Scarcity during times of business failure and natural calamities.
Scarcity caused on account of excessive consumption by the rich.

questions.explanation: In economics, scarcity does not mean absolute physical absence; it means relative scarcity—resources are finite and scarce in relation to the limitless desires and wants of individuals and society. Hence, (B) 'Relative scarcity i.e. scarcity in relation to the wants of the society.' correctly reflects Lionel Robbins' foundational definition of economics.

questions.questionText: Demand for a commodity refers to:

options.text: desire backed by ability to pay for the commodity.

the quantity demanded of that commodity at a certain price.
the quantity of the commodity demanded at a certain price during any particular period of time.

questions.explanation: In economics, effective demand requires three essential elements: a desire to acquire the good, backed by adequate purchasing power (ability to pay), and the willingness to spend at a specific price during a designated time period. Hence, (D) 'the quantity of the commodity demanded at a certain price during any particular period of time.' is correct.

Declining unemployment and rising prices

medium of exchange, unit of account, income distribution

there is strong relationship between money and price level and the quantity of money is the main determinant of the price
changes in the value of money or purchasing power of money are determined first and foremost by changes in the quantity of money in circulation

questions.unitTitle: Unit 1: The Concept of Money Demand: Important Theories
questions.questionText: Fisher’s approach and the Cambridge approach to demand for money consider

money as a means of transactions and therefore, demand for money is only transaction demand for money.
